chunks: From him, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Qutaybah al-A'sha, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the sacrifices of the Jews and the Christians, so he said: 'The sacrifice (dhabihah) is a name, and one cannot be trusted with the name except the Muslim.'

key_terms.ذَبَائِحِ: Sacrifices (plural of dhabihah, referring to slaughtered animals)
key_terms.يُؤْمَنُ: To be trusted / To be considered reliable

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on the meat of Jews and Christians regarding their method of slaughter?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies that 'dhabihah' is not an intrinsic property of the meat but a legal status conferred by the slaughterer's reliability. This ruling reflects the Shia scholarly view that while People of the Book may be permitted under specific conditions, the default presumption of trustworthiness (thiqa) for the act of sanctifying meat rests with the Muslim, distinguishing it from the mere linguistic label of slaughter.
